title: Service Degradation Orchestration Playbook — End-to-End Restoration & Customer Comms
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines a single, operationally lightweight path to detect, triage, orchestrate, and restore services during multi-component service degradations that affect inference latency, throughput, or correctness. It includes concrete commands, decision gates, on-call escalation flows, and customer communication templates.

Scope:
- Applies to multi-service degradations where the user-facing API or model responses are slower than the SLO or materially incorrect.
- Covers Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private customer instances where remediation steps are performed by Redwood SRE/Platform/Runtime teams.
- Excludes scheduled maintenance and isolated non-customer-impacting infra tasks.

Primary audience and owners:
- Primary: SRE oncall (pager) and serving-runtime oncall.
- Secondary: Platform/Autoscaling, Customer Success for impacted customers, Incident Commander (IC) for Sev1/Sev2.
- Owners: eng-sre (runbook authority), eng-serving-runtime (technical remediation), customer-success (external comms).

SLOs & severity classification (quick reference):
| Severity | Customer impact | SLO threshold (example) | Target MTTR | Immediate action | Pager escalation |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Sev1 | Global outage or >50% requests failing | 99.95% p99 latency or availability | 30m | Page oncall & IC | Phone + Slack #incident-critical |
| Sev2 | Single region degraded or >10% users affected | 99.5% p99 latency | 2h | Page oncall & create incident channel | Slack + Email to stakeholders |
| Sev3 | Localized errors, non-critical customer impact | Operational but degraded | 1 business day | Ticket, monitoring watch | Async notification |

Note: thresholds above are examples; confirm product SLOs in product-overview pages before declaring Sev.

Detection & Triage (first 10 minutes):
1) Validate alert source and deduplicate: check Prometheus alert, Sentry errors, and external customer reports.
2) Snapshot key metrics (execute saved Grafana view):
   - p50/p95/p99 latency for /v1/generate endpoint per model variant
   - request error rate (5xx) and 429s per minute
   - GPU utilization and queue length on Dedicated pools
   - Cache hit ratio for KV/prefix caching
3) Quickly confirm whether degradation is: (a) control-plane/configuration, (b) serving-runtime performance, (c) infra (network, disk), (d) model-quality/regression.
4) If impact >= Sev2: create incident channel, assign IC, and follow the orchestration checklist below.

Immediate checks & commands (copy/paste):
- Verify API gateway health:
  curl -fS https://api.redwood.internal/health || echo "gateway unhealthy"
- Check deployment pod status (k8s clusters used for Hosted API):
  kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=api-gateway -o wide
- Check runtime pod logs (tail last 200 lines):
  kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=serving-runtime --tail=200 | sed -n '1,200p'
- Query in-service queue length and KV cache hit ratio (example internal tool):
  rcli metrics get --service serving-runtime --metric queue_length
  rcli metrics get --service cache --metric hit_ratio --window 5m
- Toggle runtime verbose debugging (temporary):
  rcli runtime debug --set true --target pod/<pod-name>

Containment & mitigation decision tree:
- Decision gate A: Is the degradation tied to a single service or widespread?
  - Single service: restart that service, scale replicas, or revert recent deploy.
  - Widespread: consider cross-service fallbacks and model-level degradation.
- Decision gate B: Is the model backend CPU/GPU saturated?
  - Yes: activate emergency autoscale (if policy allows) or shift degraded traffic to lower-cost model variant.
  - No: investigate networking and control-plane throttles.

Common remediation actions (ordered by speed/risk):
1) Scale out replicas (fast, low risk):
   kubectl -n runtime scale deployment/serving-runtime --replicas=6
2) Roll back recent model or runtime release (if rollout in last 30 minutes):
   kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deployment/serving-runtime --to-revision=<previous>
3) Enable model fallback for affected route (API router toggle):
   curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $INCIDENT_TOKEN" \
     https://controlplane.internal/routes/route-id/toggle_fallback \
     -d '{"fallback_model":"gpt-mini-1","reason":"incident-{{incident_id}}"}'
4) Disable autoscaling policies that are thrashing (as last resort):
   rcli autoscale set --policy-id pol-123 --enabled false --note "incident-{{incident_id}}"
5) If KV cache cold-start causing latency: invalidate small keyspace then warm using synthetic warmers. Example invalidation:
   rcli cache invalidate --prefix "/prefix/user/" --confirm

Traffic orchestration (when rollback/scale insufficient):
- Controlled regional failover: shift X% of traffic from region A to B via routing-service API. Example:
  curl -X PATCH https://routing.internal/projects/redwood/weights -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"region_weights":{"us-east-1":0.2,"us-west-1":0.8}}'
- Degraded-mode API (graceful degradation):
  Purpose: return cached responses or shorter token limits to preserve availability.
  Example toggle (control plane):
  curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/flags/degraded_mode -H 'Authorization: Bearer $INCIDENT_TOKEN' -d '{"enabled":true,"max_output_tokens":128}'
- Model fallback pattern: route to quantized or distilled variant for latency-sensitive routes. Add telemetry tag: "fallback=true".

Customer communications (templates)
- Initial incident notification (send within 15–30 minutes for Sev1/Sev2):
  Subject: [Redwood] Incident {{incident_id}} — Degraded generation latency
  Body:
  Hello {CustomerName},

  We are investigating an issue affecting generation latency for requests to models in {region}. Our engineers have identified elevated queue times and are executing remediation steps.
  What we know now:
  - Start time: {{start_time}}
  - Impact: increased latency / partial errors for some requests
  - Affected services: API generation endpoints
  - What we’re doing: scaling runtime, enabling fallbacks, and monitoring closely
  Next update: {ETA or time window}

  If you have critical workflows impacted, reply to this email or open a support ticket and reference {{incident_id}}.

  — Redwood Incident Response

- Progress update template (every 30–60 minutes for Sev1):
  Subject: [Redwood] Incident {{incident_id}} — Update {#}
  Body: current status, actions taken, observed metrics (p99 latency, error rate), and ETA if available.

- Resolution / RCA summary template (final):
  Subject: [Redwood] Incident {{incident_id}} — Resolved / Root cause analysis
  Body: include timeline, root cause, fix applied, mitigation steps to prevent recurrence, and whether any customer data was affected. Attach postmortem link.

On-call handoff & follow-up checklist:
- Handoff must include: timeline, actions taken, who is owning follow-ups (owners and JIRA tickets), known mitigations still active (e.g., degraded_mode=true), and next scheduled update.
- Use the Handoff template in this channel: 
  - Current status:
  - Open tasks and owners:
  - Technical debt / follow-ups (create JIRA tickets with tag incident-{{incident_id}})
  - Postmortem owner assigned: @<name>

Game day exercise: service-degradation drill (quarterly)
Objective: validate the entire orchestration path from detection to customer comms for a realistic degradation event.
Pre-reqs:
- Non-production environment mirroring production topology (runtime+gateway+routing).
- Test models with same resource profiles.
- Synthetic load generator and synthetic warmers.
Exercise steps (3 hours):
1) Inject resource pressure on runtime pods (cpu/gpu) in region A.
2) Trigger alerts and verify oncall paging works.
3) Execute playbook remediation (scale, rollback, fallback) with time targets.
4) Perform controlled traffic shift via routing-service.
5) Send customer notification drafts and simulate downstream CS responses.
Success criteria:
- Incident declared within 10 min of alert.
- Primary remediation (scale or fallback) completed within 30 min.
- Communications template reach time < 30 min.

Post-incident: postmortem and measurement
- Postmortem must be written within 72 hours and include: timeline, root cause, detection gap, mitigation steps, follow-ups with owners, and SLO impact calculation.
- SLO impact calculation example: if p99 latency breached from 02:00–03:00 for 1 hour with traffic 10k reqs/min, compute error budget consumed and SLA credit owed if applicable.
- Attach graphs (Grafana snapshots) and relevant logs using internal storage links.

Dashboards & key metrics to display on the incident channel (minimum):
- /v1/generate: p50/p95/p99 latency by model variant
- Error rate (5xx) and 429s by route
- Runtime queue length and GPU memory utilization per node
- Autoscaler event stream and recent scaling actions
- Cache hit ratio and eviction rate

Runbook maintenance & governance:
- Quarterly review by eng-sre and eng-serving-runtime; update after every Sev1/Sev2 postmortem.
- Game-day exercises scheduled quarterly; participation mandatory for all oncall rotations every 12 months.
- Remove or deprecate runbook sections older than 18 months; any retained content requires verification date header.

Appendix: quick playbook cheat-sheet (one-page)
- If p99 latency spikes and 5xx rate increases: scale replicas -> check GPU memory pressure -> switch to fallback model -> toggle degraded_mode -> inform customers.
- If 5xx is only from Control Plane: confirm API key/billing & push temporary routing rule to bypass control plane checks.

Contact matrix (emergency):

- Runtime oncall lead: Rina Gupta (Slack @rina)
- Incident Commander rotation: see internal rota page

Document history and owners:

- Review cadence: quarterly or after any Sev1/Sev2 incident.

End of playbook.
